title: bug: a non-numeric, zero or negative MOE_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS throttles every MCP request the daemon serves to 1 per second, because McpAdapter parses it with a bare parseInt and RateLimiter's fallback is 1 rather than the default 100, while MOE_MCP_MAX_BATCH_SIZE in the same file falls back to its default
description:
Found by defect hunt #13 (task-cc441586). Line numbers are at HEAD f159784e.

PROBLEM (packages/moe-daemon/src/server/McpAdapter.ts)
- :15-16 read MOE_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS and MOE_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS with a bare parseInt, so `abc` becomes NaN.
- The RateLimiter constructor (:46-47) replaces any non-finite or non-positive maxRequests with **1**, not the documented default 100. It then warns "Invalid rate limiter configuration; using safe defaults" (:54).
- The sibling MOE_MCP_MAX_BATCH_SIZE in the same file goes through parsePositiveIntegerEnv (:19-29), which falls back to its default.
- One McpAdapter instance (src/index.ts:779) serves every MCP client, so a single typo throttles the whole fleet to 1 request per second, under a misleading "safe defaults" line.
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md:26 lists the variable with no invalid-value rule.

EVIDENCE
- Repro: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-cc441586/B/rateLimitEnvFallback.test.ts. Copy it into packages/moe-daemon/src/__hunt__/ of a `git archive f159784e` snapshot.
- Command: `npx vitest run src/__hunt__/rateLimitEnvFallback.test.ts`. Result: 2 failed. Verbatim:
```
MOE_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS=abc: 4/5 pings refused; {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"error":{"code":-32000,"message":"Rate limit exceeded: 1 requests per 1000ms"}}
MOE_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS=0: 4/5 pings refused; {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"error":{"code":-32000,"message":"Rate limit exceeded: 1 requests per 1000ms"}}
```
- Exposure: a guard gap, not a live incident. Only a misconfigured environment hits it, but then the effect is fleet-wide.

FIX DIRECTION
- Parse both variables with parsePositiveIntegerEnv (defaults 100 and 1000), or make RateLimiter fall back to those defaults.
- The warning names the variable and the value actually used.
- MOE_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false keeps disabling the limiter as today.

FILES and hunk ownership:
- packages/moe-daemon/src/server/McpAdapter.ts: this row owns only the env parsing (~:15-16) and the RateLimiter constructor fallback (~:36-56).
- The sibling hunt row task-5158e85b owns only the dispatch comment hunk (~:301-303). The two hunks are distinct, so worktree merge-tree lands both and no dependency is needed.
- Plus a new vitest file.
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md is held at filing time: sync it only if lanes show it free at planning time.
definitionOfDone: A non-numeric, zero or negative MOE_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS or MOE_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS falls back to its default (100 requests, 1000 ms), and the warning names the variable and the value used.
A valid override still applies (for example MOE_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_REQUESTS=5: the 6th request in one window is refused), and MOE_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false still disables the limiter.
One new vitest file covers both cases (fresh module import per env) and passes with the existing McpAdapter tests, in a snapshot outside the shared checkout.

comments.content: Filer's correction to PROBLEM: 100 requests per 1000 ms is the CODE default (McpAdapter.ts:15-16, `|| '100'` and `|| '1000'`), not a documented one. docs/CONFIGURATION.md:26 names the variables with no default and no invalid-value rule. The finding stands: bad values fall to 1, while the sibling MOE_MCP_MAX_BATCH_SIZE falls back to its default. Hunk ownership in McpAdapter.ts is shared with task-5158e85b, which owns only the dispatch comment at ~:301-303.
